decisions.reason: As a niche crate with only limited website visibility, it is somewhat vulnerable, but the tooling investment and the tendency to justify a recent launch still make management more likely to continue for now.
Its dedicated product page in both 2018 and 2019 signals comparatively high investment and public commitment, which under escalation of commitment strongly favors continuation.
A stackable plastic crate sits close to the firm’s core plastics handling business, so even without heavy promotion management is likely to keep it and interpret any weak uptake as temporary.
A rackable pallet is central to an industrial plastics portfolio, and sunk development costs plus strategic fit make withdrawal within a year relatively unlikely.
Although its visibility fell from a standalone page to a simple mention, the prior launch commitment and specialized application still give management reasons to persist rather than exit quickly.
This pallet variant appears close to the firm’s established range, and earlier dedicated promotion suggests enough commitment that management would likely keep it on the market a bit longer.
